Esjeje!,

You make good points.  I'll quote another oft-cited passage on TK's
use of the term of "leftists" and then make some rambling comments.  

TK writes:
"When we speak of leftists in  this article we have in 
mind mainly socialists, collectivists, 'politically correct' 
types, feminists, gay and disability activists, animal rights 
activists and the like."

I think TK's use of the term is the common one.  And I think
his reaction to leftists is more Rush Limbaugh-like than
we realize.  He didn't get along with his parents because
of their politics.  Limbaugh characterizes leftists in terms
of their psychological type all the time.  That's part of the
standard ad hominem attack.  Just like leftists attack rightists as
selfish.  (They are, you know).

Note that a rightist and a leftist thinks conservatives are fools, not someone
who is apolitical.

TK felt that a long essay was necessary, lest the expression
of his ideas be imprecise.   But the truth is usually simpler than that.

Here, the notion of an apolitical revolutionary is misleading --
if you are a revolutionary you are extremely political (e.g.,
for example, opposed to all technology).  I once knew a great
guy who was focused solely on the threat of nuclear war (in 1984 at
Berkeley).  I don't know that his obsessive focus was any more or less valid
than TK's.  But like TK, he was very political.  Focus on a single 
issue doesn't make it apolitical.
